translations.literal: Eleventh month: the emperor died.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor died the next month.

translations.literal: Equals sign layout marker.
translations.idiomatic: Column divider.

sentences.zh: 火沴水

translations.literal: Fire encroaching on water.
translations.idiomatic: Section heading: fire injuring water.

sentences.zh: =武帝六月，任城、魯國池水皆赤如血。

translations.literal: Wudi, sixth month: in Rencheng and Lu the pond waters all turned red as blood.
translations.idiomatic: In Wu’s sixth month pools in Rencheng and Lu ran blood-red.

sentences.zh: 案劉向說，近水沴水，聽之不聰之罰也。

translations.literal: According to Liu Xiang’s gloss, this nears water being injured by water—the punishment of hearing not clear.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xiang read red water as water harmed by its own element—deaf rule.

sentences.zh: 京房《易傳》曰：「君淫于色，賢人潛，國家危，厥異水流赤。」

translations.literal: Jing Fang’s Treatise on the Changes says: “When the lord indulges in sex, worthies hide, the state is in peril, and its anomaly is that flowing waters turn red.”
translations.idiomatic: Jing Fang links crimson streams to debauchery that drives worthies into hiding.

sentences.zh: 穆帝二月，涼州城東池中有火。

translations.literal: Mudi, second month: in Liangzhou city east of the wall fire appeared in a pool.
translations.idiomatic: In Mu’s second month flames rose from a pool east of Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 四年四月，姑臧澤水中又有火。

translations.literal: Fourth year, fourth month: again fire in the marsh waters of Guzang.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the fourth year fire danced on Guzang’s marsh.

sentences.zh: 此火沴水之妖也。

translations.literal: This was the prodigy of fire encroaching on water.
translations.idiomatic: It was the classic fire-over-water omen.

sentences.zh: 明年，張天錫殺中護軍張邕。

translations.literal: The next year Zhang Tianxi killed the palace guard commander Zhang Yong.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Zhang Tianxi slew Zhang Yong, who held military power.

sentences.zh: 邕，執政之人也。

translations.literal: Yong was a man who wielded government.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yong had been a power at court.

sentences.zh: 安帝十月，錢唐臨平湖水赤，桓玄諷吳郡使言開除以為己瑞，俄而桓玄敗。

translations.literal: Andi, tenth month: the waters of Linping Lake at Qiantang turned red; Huan Xuan prompted the Wu governor to memorialize dredging it as his own auspice; soon Huan Xuan was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Xuan forced a memorial claiming red water at Linping as his omen—then he fell.

sentences.zh: 思心之不容，是謂不聖

translations.literal: When reflective mind does not tolerate—this is called “not sagely.”
translations.idiomatic: Failure of the thinking heart to embrace counsel is classed as “lack of sageness.”

sentences.zh: 《傳》曰：「思心之不容，是謂不聖，厥咎霿，厥罰恆風，厥極凶短折。

translations.literal: The Traditions say: “When reflective mind does not tolerate, it is called not sagely; its reproof lies in fog; its punishment is constant wind; its extreme is violent early death.”
translations.idiomatic: The text lists fog, ceaseless gales, and untimely death as its penalties.

sentences.zh: 時則有脂夜之妖，時則有華孽，時則有牛禍，時則有心腹之痾，時則有黃眚黃祥，時則有金木水火沴土。

translations.literal: Then there are fat-night prodigies; then freak flowering; then ox scourges; then ailments of heart and belly; then yellow ill-omens and yellow portents; then metal, wood, fire, and water encroach on earth.
translations.idiomatic: Then come night-fats, freak blossoms, ox disasters, belly sickness, yellow bale, and the four phases injuring earth.

sentences.zh: 」思心不容，是謂不聖。

translations.literal: ” Reflective mind not tolerating is called not sagely.
translations.idiomatic: A closed mind is reckoned unwise.

sentences.zh: 思心者，心思慮也。

translations.literal: Reflective mind means the mind’s thinking and planning.
translations.idiomatic: It is the faculty of deliberation.

sentences.zh: 容，寬也。

translations.literal: Rong means breadth.
translations.idiomatic: “Rong” here means breadth of spirit.

sentences.zh: 孔子曰：「居上不寬，吾何以觀之哉！

translations.literal: Confucius said, “Those above who are not magnanimous—how am I to look upon them!”
translations.idiomatic: Confucius demanded generosity from superiors.

sentences.zh: 」言上不寬大包容，臣下則不能居聖位。

translations.literal: ” It means that if those above are not broadly inclusive, ministers cannot dwell in sagely posts.
translations.idiomatic: Without breadth from the throne, no minister can be truly wise.

sentences.zh: 貌言視聽，以心為主，四進皆失，則區霿無識，故其咎霿也。

translations.literal: Bearing, words, sight, and hearing take the mind as lord; if all four err, then foggy darkness knows nothing; therefore its reproof is fog.
translations.idiomatic: When all four senses fail the ruler, judgment turns murky as fog.

sentences.zh: 雨旱寒燠，亦以風為本，四氣皆亂，故其罰恆風也。

translations.literal: Rain, drought, cold, and heat also take wind as root; when the four qi are all disordered, therefore its punishment is constant wind.
translations.idiomatic: Weather chaos expresses itself in endless wind.

sentences.zh: 恆風傷物，故其極凶短折也。

translations.literal: Constant wind injures things; therefore its extreme is violent early death.
translations.idiomatic: Relentless wind wastes life—hence the “early death” extreme.

sentences.zh: 傷人曰凶，禽獸曰短，草木曰折。

translations.literal: Injury to people is called xiong; to birds and beasts duan; to plants zhe.
translations.idiomatic: Human death is “violent”; beasts “cut short”; plants “broken.”

sentences.zh: 一曰，凶，夭也；

translations.literal: One account says: xiong means premature death.
translations.idiomatic: Another gloss: xiong is untimely end.

sentences.zh: 兄喪弟曰短，父喪子曰折。

translations.literal: Elder brother dying and younger brother duan; father dying and son zhe.
translations.idiomatic: Brother-loss is “short”; son-loss is “broken.”

sentences.zh: 在人，腹中肥而包裹心者，脂也。

translations.literal: Extending to people, what in the belly is fat and wraps the heart is fat tissue.
translations.idiomatic: In the body, the fat that sheaths the heart is zhi.

sentences.zh: 心區霿則冥晦，故有脂夜之妖。

translations.literal: When the heart is foggy-dark then there is gloom; therefore there are fat-night prodigies.
translations.idiomatic: A benighted heart brings “fat-night” omens.

sentences.zh: 一曰，有脂物而夜為妖，若脂夜汙人衣，淫之象也。

translations.literal: One account says: there is a fatty thing and at night it is prodigious; like fat-night staining people’s clothes—an image of debauchery.
translations.idiomatic: Some read night-fats as foul smears—lust signs.

sentences.zh: 一曰，夜妖者，雲風並起而杳冥，故與常風同象也。

translations.literal: One account says: night prodigies mean wind and cloud rising together and deep gloom—therefore they share the image with constant wind.
translations.idiomatic: Others equate them with wind-driven midnight gloom.

sentences.zh: 溫而風則生螟螣，有裸蟲之孽。

translations.literal: When it is warm yet windy, then caterpillar pests are born; there are calamities of naked worms.
translations.idiomatic: Warmth mixed with wind breeds caterpillars—naked-worm scourges.

sentences.zh: 劉向以為：「于《易》，《巽》為風，為木。

translations.literal: Liu Xiang took it that “In the Changes, Xun is wind and wood.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xiang cites Hexagram Xun as wind and wood.

sentences.zh: 卦在三月四月，繼陽而治，主木之華實。

translations.literal: The hexagram governs the third and fourth months, succeeding yang and ruling, presiding over the flowering and fruiting of wood.
translations.idiomatic: It presides spring’s flowering and fruiting.

sentences.zh: 風氣盛至，秋冬木復華，故有華孽。

translations.literal: When wind qi is excessive to the utmost, in autumn and winter trees bloom again; therefore there are freak flowerings.
translations.idiomatic: When wind runs wild, trees reflower in winter—freak blossoms.

sentences.zh: 」一曰，地氣盛同秋冬復華。

translations.literal: One account says: when earth qi is abundant, likewise in autumn and winter they bloom again.
translations.idiomatic: Some blame surging earth qi for off-season blooms.

sentences.zh: 一曰，華者色也，土為內事，謂女孽也。

translations.literal: One account says: hua means color; earth is inner affairs—meaning women’s prodigies.
translations.idiomatic: Another gloss links freak flowers to feminine intrigue.

sentences.zh: 于《易》，《坤》為土，為牛。

translations.literal: In the Changes, Kun is earth and ox.
translations.idiomatic: The Changes pairs Kun with earth and the ox.

sentences.zh: 牛大心而不能思慮，心氣毀，故有牛禍。

translations.literal: The ox has a large heart yet cannot think and plan; the qi of the mind is ruined; therefore there are ox scourges.
translations.idiomatic: The ox’s dull wit mirrors a ruined mind—hence ox portents.

sentences.zh: 一曰，牛多死及為怪，亦是也。

translations.literal: One account says: in years of cold many oxen die and behave strangely; this too is such.
translations.idiomatic: Mass ox deaths in harsh winters count too.

sentences.zh: 及人，則多病心腹者，故有心腹之痾。

translations.literal: Extending to people, then many suffer heart and belly; therefore there are belly ailments.
translations.idiomatic: Among people it shows as belly and heart disease.

sentences.zh: 土色黃，故有黃眚黃祥。

translations.literal: Earth’s color is yellow; therefore there are yellow ill-omens and yellow portents.
translations.idiomatic: Earth’s hue is yellow—yellow bale follows.

sentences.zh: 凡思心傷者，病土氣；

translations.literal: Whenever reflective mind is injured, earth qi is diseased.
translations.idiomatic: A wounded mind sickens the earth phase.

sentences.zh: 土氣病，則金木水火沴之，故曰時則有金木水火沴土。

translations.literal: When earth qi is diseased, then metal, wood, fire, and water encroach on it; therefore it says then metal, wood, fire, and water encroach on earth.
translations.idiomatic: Then the other phases gang up on earth.

sentences.zh: 不言「惟」而獨曰「時則有」者，非一沖氣所沴，明其異大也。

translations.literal: It does not say “only” but alone says “then there is” because it is not one clashing qi that encroaches—making clear that the anomaly is great.
translations.idiomatic: The wording stresses many elements striking at once.

sentences.zh: 其極凶短折者，順之，其福曰考終命。

translations.literal: As for its extreme of violent early death, if one complies with it, its blessing is called “completion of years.”
translations.idiomatic: Heeding the warning turns the extreme into a full lifespan.

sentences.zh: 劉歆《思心傳》曰：「時有臝蟲之孽，謂螟螣之屬也。」

translations.literal: Liu Xin’s Treatise on Reflective Mind says: “Then there are calamities of naked worms—meaning caterpillars and the like.”
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xin classes caterpillars under naked-worm scourges.

translations.literal: Equals sign layout marker.
translations.idiomatic: Column divider.

sentences.zh: 庶徵恆風

translations.literal: Among the various signs: constant wind.
translations.idiomatic: Section heading: persistent wind.

sentences.zh: =魏齊王十一月，大風數十日，髮屋折樹。

translations.literal: Wei’s Prince of Qi, eleventh month: great wind for several tens of days; it tore off roofs and broke trees.
translations.idiomatic: Wei’s Qi prince saw weeks of gales that unroofed houses and snapped trees.

sentences.zh: 十二月戊午晦尤甚，動太極東閣。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, last day wuwu: especially severe; it shook the east pavilion of the Great Ultimate.
translations.idiomatic: On the wuwu eclipse-day the wind shook the Taiji east annex.

sentences.zh: 正月壬辰朔，西北大風，髮屋折樹木，昏塵蔽天。

translations.literal: First month, new moon renchen: great northwest wind; it tore off roofs and broke trees; dusk dust veiled heaven.
translations.idiomatic: The renchen new moon brought a northwest gale that stripped roofs and filled the sky with dust.

sentences.zh: 案管輅說，此為時刑大臣，執政之憂也。

translations.literal: According to Guan Lu’s gloss, this was punishing the seasons and executing great ministers—the worry of those who hold power.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Lu read it as heaven punishing chief ministers.

sentences.zh: 是時，曹爽區霿自專，驕僭過度，天戒數見，終不改革，此思心不睿，恆風之罰也。

translations.literal: At this time Cao Shuang was fog-dark and monopolized power, arrogant transgression beyond measure; heaven’s warnings appeared repeatedly yet he never reformed—this was reflective mind not keen and the punishment of constant wind.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Shuang’s blind arrogance drew repeated winds of warning until he was swept away.

sentences.zh: 後逾旬而爽等誅滅。

translations.literal: After more than a ten-day period Shuang and his party were executed and destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Within a fortnight Cao Shuang’s clique was exterminated.

sentences.zh: 京房《易傳》曰：「眾逆同志，至德乃潛，厥異風。

translations.literal: Jing Fang’s Treatise on the Changes says: “When the many rebel and share one mind, utmost virtue then hides; its anomaly is wind.
translations.idiomatic: Jing Fang lists omens of mass defiance that drive virtue underground.

sentences.zh: 其風也，行不解，物不長，雨小而傷。

translations.literal: Its wind: moving it does not loosen; things do not grow; rain is small yet injurious.
translations.idiomatic: Such wind stalls growth and brings spiteful drizzle.

sentences.zh: 政悖德隱茲謂亂，厥風先風不雨，大風暴起，髮屋折木。

translations.literal: Government perverse and virtue hidden—this is called disorder; its wind first blows wind without rain, then great storm arises, tearing off roofs and breaking trees.
translations.idiomatic: Tyranny without hidden virtue brings dry gales, then tempests.

sentences.zh: 守義不進茲謂眊，厥風與雲俱起，折五穀莖。

translations.literal: Keeping righteousness but not advancing—this is called dimness; its wind rises with clouds together, breaking the stalks of the five grains.
translations.idiomatic: Hesitant justice yields wind that snaps the grain.

sentences.zh: 臣易上政茲謂不順，厥風大飆髮屋。

translations.literal: Ministers altering what is above in government—this is called not compliant; its wind is great blast tearing off roofs.
translations.idiomatic: Ministerial usurpation calls down roof-ripping squalls.

sentences.zh: 賦斂不理茲謂禍，厥風絕經紀，止即溫，溫即蟲。

translations.literal: Taxes and levies not ordered—this is called calamity; its wind snaps the warp and weft; stopping then is warm, warm then insects.
translations.idiomatic: Predatory taxes bring erratic wind, warmth, and vermin.

sentences.zh: 侯專封茲謂不統，厥風疾而樹不搖，穀不成。

translations.literal: Marquises monopolizing fiefs—this is called lack of unity; its wind is swift yet trees do not sway; grain does not mature.
translations.idiomatic: Over-mighty nobles bring wind that fails to stir trees yet kills the crop.

sentences.zh: 辟不思道里茲謂無澤，厥風不搖木，旱無雲，傷禾。

translations.literal: Lords not pondering roads—this is called lack of grace; its wind does not shake trees; drought without clouds injures grain.
translations.idiomatic: Rulers who ignore the highways get windless drought that blights fields.

sentences.zh: 公常於里茲謂亂，厥風微而溫，生蟲蝗，害五穀。

translations.literal: Dukes always in the hamlet—this is called disorder; its wind is slight yet warm; insects and locusts are born, injuring the five grains.
translations.idiomatic: Absentee lords breed warm breezes and locusts.

sentences.zh: 棄政作淫茲謂惑，厥風溫，螟蟲起，害有益人之物。

translations.literal: Casting aside government and making debauchery—this is called delusion; its wind is warm; blight worms arise, injuring things that benefit people.
translations.idiomatic: Neglect of duty for pleasure brings warm wind and caterpillars.

sentences.zh: 諸侯不朝茲謂畔，厥風無恆，地變赤，雨殺人。」

translations.literal: When feudal lords do not court—this is called rebellion; its wind has no constancy; earth changes red; rain kills people.”
translations.idiomatic: When lords shun court, wind shifts wildly, earth reddens, and killing rain falls.

sentences.zh: 吳孫權八月朔，大風，江海湧溢，平地水深八尺，拔高陵樹二千株，石碑蹉動，吳城兩門飛落。

translations.literal: Wu Sun Quan, eighth month new moon: great wind; rivers and seas surged and overflowed; on level ground water was eight chi deep; it uprooted two thousand trees on the Gaoling mound; stone steles shifted; two gates of Wu city flew off.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan’s eighth-month gale flooded the coast eight feet deep, tore two thousand trees on Gaoling, shifted steles, and blew off two city gates.

sentences.zh: 案華核對，役繁賦重，區霿不容之罰也。

translations.literal: According to Hua He’s check, this was the punishment of corvée being heavy and taxes great, fog-dark mind not tolerating.
translations.idiomatic: Hua He blamed crushing labor and taxes—mind too cramped for mercy.

sentences.zh: 明年，權薨。

translations.literal: The next year Quan died.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan died the next year.

sentences.zh: 孫亮十二月丙申，大風震電。

translations.literal: Sun Liang, twelfth month bingshen: great wind and shaking lightning.
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen in Sun Liang’s twelfth month came a thunderstorm.

sentences.zh: 是歲，魏遣大眾三道來攻，諸葛恪破其東興軍，二軍亦退。

translations.literal: That year Wei sent a great host in three roads to attack; Zhuge Ke broke their Dongxing army; the two other armies also withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Wei invaded on three fronts; Zhuge Ke routed Dongxing; the rest retreated.

sentences.zh: 明年，恪又攻新城，喪眾太半，還，伏誅。

translations.literal: The next year Ke again attacked Xincheng, lost more than half his host, returned, and was executed in secret.
translations.idiomatic: Ke besieged Xincheng next year, lost half his army, and was assassinated on return.

sentences.zh: 孫休十一月甲午，風四轉五復，蒙霧連日。

translations.literal: Sun Xiu, eleventh month jiawu: wind turned four ways and returned five times; mist blanketed for successive days.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu under Sun Xiu the wind veered and mist hung for days.

sentences.zh: 是時，孫綝一門五侯，權傾吳主，風霧之災，與漢五侯、丁、傅同應也。

translations.literal: At this time within Sun Lin’s one gate there were five marquises; power tilted against the Wu ruler—the disaster of wind and mist matched Han’s five marquises and Ding and Fu.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Lin’s clan held five marquises and overshadowed the king—the same wind-and-mist answer as the five Wangs and the Ding and Fu consorts of Han.

sentences.zh: 十二月丁卯夜，有大風，發木揚沙。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, night of dingmao: great wind; it tore up trees and raised sand.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao’s night a gale uprooted timber and whipped sand.

sentences.zh: 明日，綝誅。

translations.literal: The next day Sun Lin was executed.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Lin died the next day.

sentences.zh: 武帝五月辛卯朔，廣平大風，折木。

translations.literal: Wudi, fifth month, new moon xinmao: in Guangping great wind, breaking trees.
translations.idiomatic: On the xinmao new moon of Wu’s fifth month Guangping’s wind snapped trees.

sentences.zh: 五月，下邳、廣陵大風，壞千餘家，折樹木。

translations.literal: Fifth month: in Xiapi and Guangling great wind, ruining over a thousand homes, breaking trees.
translations.idiomatic: That fifth month Xiapi and Guangling gales wrecked a thousand houses.

sentences.zh: 其月甲申，廣陵、司吾、下邳大風，折木。

translations.literal: That month jiashen: in Guangling, Siwu, and Xiapi great wind, breaking trees.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen Guangling, Siwu, and Xiapi saw wind that broke trees.

sentences.zh: 三年八月，河間大風，折木。

translations.literal: Third year, eighth month: in Hejian great wind, breaking trees.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year’s eighth month Hejian’s storm snapped trees.

sentences.zh: 五月，濟南暴風，折木，傷麥。

translations.literal: Fifth month: in Jinan a violent wind broke trees and injured wheat.
translations.idiomatic: Jinan’s fifth-month squall ruined the wheat.

sentences.zh: 六月，高平大風，折木，發壞邸閣四十餘區。

translations.literal: Sixth month: in Gaoping great wind, breaking trees, tearing and ruining more than forty granary compounds.
translations.idiomatic: Gaoping’s sixth-month gale wrecked over forty state granaries.

sentences.zh: 七月，上黨又大風，傷秋稼。

translations.literal: Seventh month: in Shangdang again great wind, injuring autumn crops.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Shangdang was hit again by gales that ruined the late harvest.

sentences.zh: 八年六月，郡國八大風。

translations.literal: Eighth year, sixth month: in eight commanderies and kingdoms great wind.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the eighth year eight provinces were swept by violent winds.

sentences.zh: 九年正月，京都風雹，髮屋拔樹。

translations.literal: Ninth year, first month: in the capital district wind and hail tore off roofs and uprooted trees.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the ninth year a hail-laced storm stripped the capital’s roofs and toppled trees.

sentences.zh: 後二年，宮車晏駕。

translations.literal: After two years the palace carriage passed at dusk (the emperor died).
translations.idiomatic: Two years later the emperor died.

sentences.zh: 惠帝六月，大風雨，拔木。

translations.literal: Huidi, sixth month: great wind and rain, uprooting trees.
translations.idiomatic: In Emperor Hui’s sixth month a tempest uprooted trees.

sentences.zh: 五年四月庚寅夜，暴風，城東渠波浪殺人。

translations.literal: Fifth year, fourth month, night of gengyin: violent wind; waves in the ditch east of the city killed people.
translations.idiomatic: On the night of gengyin in the fourth month of the fifth year a squall whipped the eastern moat into waves that drowned people.

sentences.zh: 七月，下邳大風，壞廬舍。

translations.literal: Seventh month: in Xiapi great wind, ruining huts and houses.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Xiapi’s gale wrecked dwellings.

sentences.zh: 九月，雁門、新興、太原、上黨災風傷稼。

translations.literal: Ninth month: in Yanmen, Xinxing, Taiyuan, and Shangdang calamitous wind injured crops.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month freak winds across Yanmen, Xinxing, Taiyuan, and Shangdang battered the fields.

sentences.zh: 明年，氐羌反叛，大兵西討。

translations.literal: The next year the Di and Qiang rebelled; a great host marched west to punish them.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Di and Qiang tribes rose in revolt and imperial armies marched west.

sentences.zh: 九年六月，飆風吹賈謐朝服飛數百丈。

translations.literal: Ninth year, sixth month: a whirlwind blew Jia Mi’s court robes flying several hundred zhang.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the ninth year a gust snatched Jia Mi’s court dress and carried it hundreds of yards through the air.

sentences.zh: 明年，謐誅。

translations.literal: The next year Mi was executed.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Mi was put to death the following year.

sentences.zh: 十一月甲子朔，京都連大風，髮屋折木。

translations.literal: Eleventh month, new moon jiazi: in the capital district successive great winds tore off roofs and broke trees.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiazi new moon the capital suffered day after day of gales that unroofed houses and snapped trees.

sentences.zh: 十二月，湣懷太子廢，幽於許昌。

translations.literal: Twelfth month: Crown Prince Minhuai was deposed and confined at Xuchang.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month the heir Minhuai was cast down and imprisoned at Xuchang.

sentences.zh: 二月，大風拔木。

translations.literal: Second month: great wind uprooted trees.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month a gale tore up trees.

sentences.zh: 三月，湣懷被害。

translations.literal: Third month: Minhuai was murdered.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month Crown Prince Minhuai was killed.

sentences.zh: 己卯，喪柩發許昌還洛。

translations.literal: Day jimao: the funeral bier set out from Xuchang back to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: On jimao the prince’s coffin left Xuchang for Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 是日，又大風雷電，幃蓋飛裂。

translations.literal: That day again great wind, thunder, and lightning; curtains and canopies flew apart and tore.
translations.idiomatic: That same day brought another thunderstorm that shredded the funeral banners and shades.

sentences.zh: 四月，張華第舍飆風起，折木飛繒，折軸六七。

translations.literal: Fourth month: at Zhang Hua’s residence a whirlwind arose, broke trees and sent silk flying, and broke six or seven axles.
translations.idiomatic: In April a cyclone struck Zhang Hua’s compound, snapped trees, whipped silk through the air, and shattered six or seven cart axles.

sentences.zh: 是月，華遇害。

translations.literal: That month Hua met murder.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hua was assassinated that month.

sentences.zh: 十一月戊午朔，大風從西北來，折木飛沙石，六日止。

translations.literal: Eleventh month, new moon wuwu: great wind came from the northwest, breaking trees and flying sand and stone; it stopped after six days.
translations.idiomatic: On the wuwu new moon a six-day northwest gale drove sand and broke timber.

sentences.zh: 明年正月，趙王倫篡位。

translations.literal: First month of the next year: Prince Zhao Lun usurped the throne.
translations.idiomatic: The following first month Prince Zhao Lun seized the throne.

sentences.zh: 八月，郡國三大風。

translations.literal: Eighth month: in three commanderies and kingdoms great wind.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month three provinces were swept by high winds.

sentences.zh: 正月乙丑，西北大風。

translations.literal: First month, day yichou: great northwest wind.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou in the first month a fierce northwest wind blew.

sentences.zh: 趙王倫建始元年正月癸酉，趙土倫祠太廟，災風暴起，塵四合。

translations.literal: Prince Zhao Lun, Jianshi first year, first month, day guiyou: when Zhao Prince Lun sacrificed at the Grand Temple, a calamitous wind suddenly arose and dust closed in from four sides (the name is written with the earth radical where the text expects the jade radical for prince).
translations.idiomatic: On guiyou when Prince Zhao Lun worshipped at the Grand Temple, a freak wind whipped dust until the sky closed in—the manuscript miswrites the title graph for prince.

sentences.zh: 其年四月，倫伏辜。

translations.literal: That year, fourth month: Lun suffered execution for his crimes.
translations.idiomatic: Lun was executed in the fourth month that year.

sentences.zh: 元帝七月丙寅，大風拔木，屋瓦皆飛。

translations.literal: Yuandi, seventh month, day bingyin: great wind uprooted trees; roof tiles all flew.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin in Emperor Yuan’s seventh month a gale tore up trees and sent tiles flying.

sentences.zh: 八月，暴風壞屋，拔御道柳樹百餘株。

translations.literal: Eighth month: violent wind ruined houses and uprooted more than a hundred willows along the imperial avenue.
translations.idiomatic: In August a squall wrecked buildings and ripped out over a hundred willows lining the imperial road.

sentences.zh: 其風縱橫無常，若風自八方來者。

translations.literal: Its wind crossed and ran without constancy, as if wind came from the eight directions.
translations.idiomatic: The gusts veered wildly, as though eight winds struck at once.

sentences.zh: 是時，王敦專權，害尚書令刁協、僕射周顗等，故風縱橫若非一處也。

translations.literal: At this time Wang Dun monopolized power and harmed Director of the Secretariat Diao Xie, Vice Director Zhou Yi, and others; therefore the wind crossed as if not from one place.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun was then killing Diao Xie and Zhou Yi—hence the wind seemed to blow from every quarter.

sentences.zh: 此臣易上政，諸侯不朝之罰也。

translations.literal: This is the punishment of ministers altering government above and feudal lords not attending court.
translations.idiomatic: It answered ministerial usurpation and lords who shunned court.

sentences.zh: 十一月，宮車晏駕。

translations.literal: Eleventh month: the palace carriage passed at dusk.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor died in the eleventh month.

sentences.zh: 成帝三月壬辰，成都大風，髮屋折木。

translations.literal: Chengdi, third month, day renchen: in Chengdu great wind tore off roofs and broke trees.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen in Emperor Cheng’s third month Chengdu suffered a storm that stripped roofs and snapped trees.

sentences.zh: 四月，李壽襲殺李期，自立。

translations.literal: Fourth month: Li Shou attacked and killed Li Qi and set himself up.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month Li Shou murdered Li Qi and seized Cheng-Han’s throne.

sentences.zh: 穆帝八月丁未，策立皇后何氏。

translations.literal: Mudi, eighth month, day dingwei: by edict they established Empress He.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei in Emperor Mu’s eighth month Lady He was enthroned as empress.

sentences.zh: 是日，疾風。

translations.literal: That day: violent wind.
translations.idiomatic: A sharp gale blew that same day.

sentences.zh: 後桓玄篡位，乃降後為零陵縣君，不睿之罰也。

translations.literal: Afterward Huan Xuan usurped the throne and then demoted the empress to Lady of Lingling county—the punishment of not being sagely.
translations.idiomatic: When Huan Xuan seized power he reduced Empress He to a county lady—the omen of an unwise heart.

sentences.zh: 五年正月戊戌朔，疾風。

translations.literal: Fifth year, first month, new moon wuxu: violent wind.
translations.idiomatic: On the wuxu new moon of the fifth year a fierce wind struck.

sentences.zh: 海西公二月，大風迅急，是年被廢。

translations.literal: Marquis of Haixi, second month: great wind, swift and urgent; that year he was deposed.
translations.idiomatic: In the deposed emperor of Haixi’s second month came racing gales; he was cast down that year.

sentences.zh: 孝武帝三月，京都大風，火大起。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu, third month: in the capital district great wind; fire greatly arose.
translations.idiomatic: In Emperor Wu’s third month the capital was rocked by wind and great fires broke out.

sentences.zh: 是時，桓溫入朝，志在陵上，帝又幼少，人懷憂恐，斯不睿之徵也。

translations.literal: At this time Huan Wen entered court with intent to encroach upon those above; the emperor was again young; people harbored worry and fear—this was a sign of not being sagely.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen had marched to the capital to bully the throne while the boy emperor inspired dread—tokens of collective unwisdom.

sentences.zh: 三年三月戊申朔，暴風迅起，從醜上來，須臾逆轉，從子上來，飛沙揚礫。

translations.literal: Third year, third month, new moon wushen: violent wind rose swiftly, coming from above chou; in a moment it reversed and came from above zi, flying sand and raising gravel.
translations.idiomatic: On the wushen new moon a cyclone sprang from the northeast branch azimuth, then suddenly whirled to strike from the north, driving sand and stones.

sentences.zh: 二月乙丑朔，暴風折木。

translations.literal: Second month, new moon yichou: violent wind broke trees.
translations.idiomatic: The yichou new moon brought a squall that snapped trees.

sentences.zh: 閏三月甲子朔，暴風疾雨俱至，髮屋折木。

translations.literal: Intercalary third month, new moon jiazi: violent wind and swift rain both arrived, tearing off roofs and breaking trees.
translations.idiomatic: On the intercalary jiazi new moon wind and driving rain together stripped roofs and broke timber.

sentences.zh: 三年六月，長安大風，拔苻堅宮中樹。

translations.literal: Third year, sixth month: in Chang’an great wind uprooted trees in Fu Jian’s palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the third year Chang’an’s gale tore trees from Fu Jian’s palace grounds.

sentences.zh: 其後，堅再南伐，遂有淝水之敗，身戮國亡。

translations.literal: Afterward Jian again campaigned south, then had the defeat at the Fei River; his person was slain and the state perished.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian’s second southern campaign ended at Feishui; he died and his kingdom fell.

sentences.zh: 四年八月乙未，暴風揚沙石。

translations.literal: Fourth year, eighth month, day yiwei: violent wind raised sand and stones.
translations.idiomatic: On yiwei in the fourth year’s eighth month a sandstorm struck.

sentences.zh: 十二年正月壬子夜，暴風。

translations.literal: Twelfth year, first month, night of renzi: violent wind.
translations.idiomatic: On the night of renzi in the twelfth year’s first month a violent wind blew.

sentences.zh: 七月甲辰，大風折木。

translations.literal: Seventh month, day jiachen: great wind broke trees.
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen in the seventh month a gale snapped trees.

sentences.zh: 十三年十二月乙未，大風，晝晦。

translations.literal: Thirteenth year, twelfth month, day yiwei: great wind; daytime grew dark.
translations.idiomatic: On yiwei in the thirteenth year’s twelfth month a wind darkened the noon sky.

sentences.zh: 其後帝崩而諸侯違命，權奪於元顯，禍成于桓玄，是其應也。

translations.literal: Afterward the emperor died and the feudal lords defied commands; power was seized by Yuan Xian; disaster was completed by Huan Xuan—this was its response.
translations.idiomatic: After his death lords defied orders, Sima Yuanxian seized power, and Huan Xuan finished the ruin—the omen answered.

sentences.zh: 十七年六月乙卯，大風折木。

translations.literal: Seventeenth year, sixth month, day yimao: great wind broke trees.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao in the seventeenth year’s sixth month a gale snapped trees.

sentences.zh: 安帝二月甲辰夜，大風雨，大航門屋瓦飛落。

translations.literal: Andi, second month, night of jiachen: great wind and rain; roof tiles of the Great Bridge Gate flew and fell.
translations.idiomatic: On the night of jiachen in Emperor An’s second month a storm tore tiles from the Great Bridge Gate.

sentences.zh: 明年，桓玄篡位，由此門入。

translations.literal: The next year Huan Xuan usurped the throne and entered through this gate.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Huan Xuan seized power and marched in through that very gate.

sentences.zh: 三年正月，桓玄出遊大航南，飄風飛其䡟輗蓋，經三月而玄敗歸江陵。

translations.literal: Third year, first month: Huan Xuan went out to tour south of the Great Bridge; a squall blew away his carriage canopy and yoke-bow cover; after three months Xuan was defeated and returned to Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the third year Huan Xuan paraded south of the Great Bridge; a gust tore off his carriage hood, and three months later he fled defeated to Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 五月，江陵又大風折木。

translations.literal: Fifth month: in Jiangling again great wind broke trees.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Jiangling was again hit by tree-snapping winds.

sentences.zh: 是月，桓玄敗于崢嶸洲，身亦屠裂。

translations.literal: That month Huan Xuan was defeated at Zhengrong Isle; his person was also dismembered.
translations.idiomatic: That same month Huan Xuan lost the battle on Zhengrong Isle and died under the blade.

sentences.zh: 十一月丁酉，大風，江陵多死者。

translations.literal: Eleventh month, day dingyou: great wind; in Jiangling many died.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou in the eleventh month a gale killed many in Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 十一月辛卯朔，西北疾風起。

translations.literal: Eleventh month, new moon xinmao: violent wind rose from the northwest.
translations.idiomatic: On the xinmao new moon a northwest gale sprang up.

sentences.zh: 五年閏十月丁亥，大風髮屋。

translations.literal: Fifth year, intercalary tenth month, day dinghai: great wind tore off roofs.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai in the intercalary tenth month of the fifth year wind stripped roofs.

sentences.zh: 明年，盧循至蔡洲。

translations.literal: The next year Lu Xun reached Cai Isle.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Lu Xun’s fleet closed on Cai Isle.

sentences.zh: 六年五月壬申，大風拔北郊樹，樹幾百年也。

translations.literal: Sixth year, fifth month, day renshen: great wind uprooted trees at the northern suburb sacrifice; the trees were nearly a hundred years old.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen in the sixth year’s fifth month a gale tore ancient trees from the northern suburban altar.

sentences.zh: 並吹琅邪、揚州二射堂倒壞。

translations.literal: Together it blew down the two archery halls of Langye and Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: It flattened the Langye and Yangzhou archery halls.

sentences.zh: 是日，盧循大艦漂沒。

translations.literal: That day Lu Xun’s great ships drifted under and were lost.
translations.idiomatic: That day Lu Xun’s great war junks were sunk by the storm.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，又風，髮屋折木。

translations.literal: Day jiaxu: again wind, tearing off roofs and breaking trees.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu another gale unroofed houses and broke trees.

sentences.zh: 是冬，王師南討。

translations.literal: That winter the royal army campaigned south.
translations.idiomatic: That winter imperial troops marched south against Lu Xun.

sentences.zh: 九年正月，大風，白馬寺浮圖刹柱折壞。

translations.literal: Ninth year, first month: great wind; the finial pillar of the White Horse Monastery pagoda broke and was ruined.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year’s first month wind snapped the spire mast of Luoyang’s White Horse Monastery stupa.

sentences.zh: 十年四月己丑朔，大風拔木。

translations.literal: Tenth year, fourth month, new moon jichou: great wind uprooted trees.
translations.idiomatic: On the jichou new moon of the tenth year’s fourth month a gale tore up trees.

sentences.zh: 六月辛亥，大風拔木。

translations.literal: Sixth month, day xinhai: great wind uprooted trees.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai in the sixth month another wind uprooted trees.

sentences.zh: 七月，淮北大風，壞廬舍。

translations.literal: Seventh month: north of the Huai great wind, ruining huts and houses.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month gales north of the Huai wrecked homes.

sentences.zh: 明年，西討司馬休之應。

translations.literal: The next year: the correspondence of the western campaign against Sima Xiuzhi.
translations.idiomatic: The next year answered with the expedition against Sima Xiuzhi.

translations.literal: Equals sign layout marker.
translations.idiomatic: Column divider in the transmitted layout.

sentences.zh: 夜妖

translations.literal: Night prodigies.
translations.idiomatic: Section heading: nocturnal anomalies.

sentences.zh: =魏高貴鄉公正月戊戌，景帝討毌丘儉，大風晦暝，行者皆頓伏，近夜妖也。

translations.literal: Wei Duke of Gaoxiang Township, first month wuxu: Emperor Jing campaigned against Guanqiu Jian; great wind darkened noon; travelers all crouched prostrate—near to a night prodigy.
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu when Sima Shi marched against Guanqiu Jian, noon turned black as night and travelers dropped flat—a classic night-omen.

sentences.zh: 劉向曰：「正晝而暝，陰為陽，臣制君也。」

translations.literal: Liu Xiang said: “When broad daylight grows dark, yin acts for yang—ministers control the lord.”
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xiang read noon darkness as ministers overshadowing their ruler.

sentences.zh: 元帝十月，京都大震，晝晦，此夜妖也。

translations.literal: Yuandi, tenth month: in the capital great shaking; daytime dark—this was a night prodigy.
translations.idiomatic: In Emperor Yuan’s tenth month the capital quaked and daylight failed—a night anomaly.

sentences.zh: 班固曰：「夜妖者，雲風並起而杳冥，故與常風同象也。

translations.literal: Ban Gu said: “Night prodigies mean wind and cloud rise together and are deep dark; therefore they share the image with constant wind.
translations.idiomatic: Ban Gu explained night omens as wind and cloud blotting the sky—kin to ceaseless wind signs.

sentences.zh: 」劉向《春秋說》云：「天戒若曰，勿使大夫世官，將令專事。

translations.literal: ” Liu Xiang’s Gloss on the Spring and Autumn says: “Heaven’s warning is as if to say, ‘Do not let great officers hold hereditary posts; they will monopolize affairs.’
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xiang’s Chunqiu gloss warns against hereditary ministerial houses monopolizing power.

sentences.zh: 暝晦，公室卑矣。

translations.literal: Dark gloom—the ducal house is low.
translations.idiomatic: Darkened daylight means the ruling house has grown feeble.

sentences.zh: 」魏見此妖，晉有天下之應也。

translations.literal: ” Wei saw this prodigy; it was the response that Jin would possess the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Wei’s night omen foretold Jin’s takeover of the realm.

sentences.zh: 懷帝十月辛卯，晝昏，至於庚子，此夜妖也。

translations.literal: Huaidi, tenth month, day xinmao: daytime gloom until gengzi day—this was a night prodigy.
translations.idiomatic: From xinmao to gengzi in Emperor Huai’s tenth month the sun stayed dim—a night portent.

sentences.zh: 後年，劉曜寇洛川，王師頻為賊所敗，帝蒙塵於平陽。

translations.literal: The year after, Liu Yao raided the Luo basin; the royal army repeatedly was defeated by the bandits; the emperor suffered dust on his robes at Pingyang.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Liu Yao struck the Luoyang region, imperial troops kept losing, and the emperor fell captive at Pingyang.

sentences.zh: 孝武帝十二月乙未，大風晦暝。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu, twelfth month, day yiwei: great wind, dark gloom.
translations.idiomatic: On yiwei in Emperor Wu’s twelfth month a wind blotted out the light.

sentences.zh: 其後帝崩，而諸侯違命，干戈內侮，權奪於元顯，禍成于桓玄。

translations.literal: Afterward the emperor died, and the feudal lords defied commands; weapons insulted those within; power was seized by Yuan Xian; disaster was completed by Huan Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: After he died lords rebelled, civil war flared, Yuanxian seized power, and Huan Xuan brought catastrophe.

translations.literal: Equals sign layout marker.
translations.idiomatic: Column divider.

sentences.zh: 臝蟲之孽

translations.literal: Calamities of naked worms.
translations.idiomatic: Section heading: naked-creature scourges.

sentences.zh: =《京房易傳》曰：「臣安祿位茲謂貪，厥災蟲食根。

translations.literal: Jing Fang’s Treatise on the Changes says: “When ministers are content in emolument posts, this is called greed; its disaster is worms eating roots.
translations.idiomatic: Jing Fang warns that complacent ministers draw root-eating pests.

sentences.zh: 德無常茲謂煩，蟲食葉。

translations.literal: When virtue lacks constancy, this is called vexation; worms eat leaves.
translations.idiomatic: Fickle virtue brings caterpillars that strip leaves.

sentences.zh: 不絀無德，蟲食本。

translations.literal: When there is no dismissal of the lacking in virtue, worms eat the root.
translations.idiomatic: Failing to remove the unworthy invites pests at the root.

sentences.zh: 與東作爭茲謂不時，蟲食莖。

translations.literal: Contending with eastern works, this is called untimeliness; worms eat stalks.
translations.idiomatic: Forcing spring labor out of season lets borers eat the stalks.

sentences.zh: 蔽惡生孽，蟲食心。」

translations.literal: Covering evil breeds prodigies; worms eat the heart.”
translations.idiomatic: Concealed wickedness breeds vermin that devour the heart.”

sentences.zh: 武帝咸甯元年七月，郡國螟。

translations.literal: Wudi, Xianning first year, seventh month: in commanderies and kingdoms crop-worms.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of Xianning 1 under Emperor Wu locust larvae swept the provinces.

sentences.zh: 九月。

translations.literal: Ninth month.
translations.idiomatic: The ninth month followed.

sentences.zh: 青州又螟。

translations.literal: In Qingzhou again crop-worms.
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhou was hit again by blight worms.

sentences.zh: 是月，郡國有青蟲食其禾稼。

translations.literal: That month, in commanderies and kingdoms there were green insects eating their grain crops.
translations.idiomatic: That month green caterpillars devoured grain across many provinces.

sentences.zh: 四年，司、冀、兗、豫、荊、揚郡國二十螟。

translations.literal: Fourth year: in twenty commanderies and kingdoms of Si, Ji, Yan, Yu, Jing, and Yang, crop-worms.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year twenty provinces along the Si–Yang belt suffered blight.

sentences.zh: ，會稽彭蜞及蟹皆化為鼠，甚眾，復大食稻為災。

translations.literal: (Continuing) In Kuaiji mud crabs and crabs all changed into rats, very many, and again greatly ate rice as a calamity.
translations.idiomatic: In Kuaiji fiddler crabs and true crabs turned into swarms of rats that devoured the rice.

sentences.zh: 九年八月，郡國二十四螟。

translations.literal: Ninth year, eighth month: in twenty-four commanderies and kingdoms crop-worms.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the ninth year twenty-four provinces reported blight.

sentences.zh: 九月，蟲又傷秋稼。

translations.literal: Ninth month: insects again injured autumn crops.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month worms ruined the late harvest again.

sentences.zh: 是時，帝聽讒諛，寵任賈充、楊駿，故有蟲蝗之災，不絀無德之罰。

translations.literal: At this time the emperor listened to slander and flattery and favored Jia Chong and Yang Jun; therefore there were disasters of insects and locusts—the punishment of not dismissing the lacking in virtue.
translations.idiomatic: The court indulged slanderers and empowered Jia Chong and Yang Jun—hence locusts answered the failure to purge the unworthy.

sentences.zh: 惠帝九月，帶方等六縣螟，食禾葉盡。

translations.literal: Huidi, ninth month: in Daifang and six other counties crop-worms; they ate every rice leaf.
translations.idiomatic: In Emperor Hui’s ninth month blight worms in Daifang and six neighboring counties stripped every rice blade.

sentences.zh: 永甯元年七月，梁、益、涼三州螟。

translations.literal: Yongning first year, seventh month: in Liang, Yi, and Liang provinces crop-worms.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of Yongning 1 blight struck Liang, Yi, and Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 是時，齊王冏執政，貪苛之應也。

translations.literal: At this time Prince of Qi Si held power—the response to greed and harshness.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Sima Jiong’s regime matched the greedy-rule omen.

sentences.zh: 十月，南安、巴西、江陽、太原、新興、北海青蟲食禾葉，甚者十傷五六。

translations.literal: Tenth month: in Nan’an, Ba-Xi, Jiangyang, Taiyuan, Xinxing, and Beihai green insects ate rice leaves; in severe cases five or six in ten were injured.
translations.idiomatic: October saw green caterpillars ravage six commanderies, often destroying more than half the crop.

sentences.zh: 十二月，郡國六螟。

translations.literal: Twelfth month: in six commanderies and kingdoms crop-worms.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month six provinces reported blight.

translations.literal: Equals sign layout marker.
translations.idiomatic: Column divider.

sentences.zh: 牛禍

translations.literal: Ox scourges.
translations.idiomatic: Section heading: bovine portents.

sentences.zh: =武帝，幽州塞北有死牛頭語，近牛禍也。

translations.literal: Wudi: north of the passes in Youzhou a dead ox’s head spoke—near an ox scourge.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Wu a dead ox’s head beyond the Youzhou frontier spoke—a bovine omen.

sentences.zh: 是時，帝多疾病，深以後事為念，而託付不以至公，思瞀亂之應也。

translations.literal: At this time the emperor was often ill and deeply anxious about later affairs, yet his entrustments were not with utmost fairness—the response of confused thinking.
translations.idiomatic: The ailing emperor’s unfair choice of heirs matched the omen of muddled judgment.

sentences.zh: 案師曠曰：「怨讟動於人。

translations.literal: According to Music Master Kuang: 'When resentful slander stirs among people,
translations.idiomatic: Shi Kuang said when malice stirs among the people,

sentences.zh: 則有非言之物而言。

translations.literal: then there are things that should not speak yet speak.'
translations.idiomatic: creatures that should not speak will speak.

sentences.zh: 」又其義也。

translations.literal: ' Again its meaning.
translations.idiomatic: That gloss fits the case.

sentences.zh: 京房《易傳》曰：「殺無罪，牛生妖。」

translations.literal: Jing Fang’s Treatise on the Changes says: 'When the guiltless are killed, oxen produce portents.'
translations.idiomatic: Jing Fang warns that executing innocents brings ox prodigies.

sentences.zh: 惠帝太安中，江夏張騁所乘牛言曰：「天下亂，乘我何之！

translations.literal: Under Emperor Hui in the Tai’an era, in Jiangxia the ox ridden by Zhang Cheng said: 'The realm is in chaos—why ride me anywhere!'
translations.idiomatic: In Tai’an years Zhang Cheng’s mount in Jiangxia suddenly demanded why it was ridden in a collapsing age.

sentences.zh: 」騁懼而還，犬又言曰：「歸何早也？

translations.literal: ' Cheng was afraid and turned back; then a dog also said: 'Why return so early?'
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Cheng fled homeward; even his dog reproached him for returning too soon.

sentences.zh: 」尋後牛又人立而行。

translations.literal: ' Soon afterward the ox again stood like a man and walked.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the ox walked upright like a man.

sentences.zh: 騁使善卜者卦之，謂曰：「天下將有兵亂，為禍非止一家。

translations.literal: Cheng had a skilled diviner cast the hexagrams; he told him: 'There will be military turmoil in the realm; the harm will not stop at one house.'
translations.idiomatic: A diviner warned Zhang Cheng that war would engulf more than his own household.

sentences.zh: 」其年，張昌反，先略江夏，騁為將帥，於是五州殘亂，騁亦族滅。

translations.literal: ' That year Zhang Chang rebelled, first raiding Jiangxia; Cheng became a commander; then five provinces were ruined in turmoil and Cheng’s clan was exterminated too.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chang rose that year, seized Jiangxia, made Zhang Cheng a general, and five provinces burned until Cheng’s kin were wiped out.

sentences.zh: 京房「易傳」曰：「牛能言，如其言占吉凶。

translations.literal: Jing Fang’s 'Treatise on the Changes' says: 'When an ox can speak, divine good or ill according to its words.'
translations.idiomatic: Jing Fang says a talking ox must be read for its prophecy.

sentences.zh: 」《易萌氣樞》曰：「人君不好士，走馬被文繡，犬狼食人食，則有六畜談言。

translations.literal: ' The Pivot of Mists in the Changes says: 'When the lord of men does not love scholars, when racing horses wear brocade and dogs and wolves eat human food, then the six domestic animals talk.'
translations.idiomatic: The Yimeng qishu adds that when rulers despise scholars yet pamper beasts, livestock will speak.

sentences.zh: 」時天子諸侯不以惠下為務，又其應也。

translations.literal: ' At that time Son of Heaven and feudal lords did not make kindness to those below their task—again its response.
translations.idiomatic: Sons of Heaven and lords had ceased caring for the people—another match for the omen.

sentences.zh: 元帝七月，晉陵陳門才牛生犢，一體兩頭。

translations.literal: Yuandi, seventh month: at Jinling in the Chen gate lane a cow calved a calf, one body with two heads.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuan’s seventh month a two-headed calf was born at a Jinling byway.

sentences.zh: 案京房《易傳》言：「牛生子二首一身，天下將分之象也。

translations.literal: According to Jing Fang’s Treatise on the Changes: 'When an ox bears a calf with two heads on one body, it is the image that the realm will split.'
translations.idiomatic: Jing Fang reads a two-headed calf as a realm split in two.

sentences.zh: 」是時，湣帝蒙塵於平陽，尋為逆胡所殺。

translations.literal: ' At this time Emperor Min suffered dust on his robes at Pingyang; soon he was killed by rebel Hu.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Min was then a captive at Pingyang and soon murdered by barbarian rebels.

sentences.zh: 元帝即位江東，天下分為二，是其應也。

translations.literal: Yuandi took the throne east of the River; the realm was divided in two—this was its response.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Rui enthroned himself south of the Yangzi while the north was lost—the sign fulfilled.

sentences.zh: ，武昌太守王諒牛生子，兩頭八足，兩尾共一腹，三年後死。

translations.literal: (Continuing) The governor of Wuchang, Wang Liang, had an ox bear a calf with two heads, eight feet, two tails sharing one belly; after three years it died.
translations.idiomatic: Wuchang governor Wang Liang’s cow dropped a monster calf—two heads, eight legs, twin tails on one belly—that died within three years.

sentences.zh: 又有牛一足三尾，皆生而死。

translations.literal: Again there was an ox with one foot and three tails; all were born and died.
translations.idiomatic: Another cow bore a one-legged, three-tailed calf that perished at birth.

sentences.zh: 案司馬彪說，「兩頭者，政在私門，上下無別之象也。

translations.literal: According to Sima Biao’s gloss, 'Two heads mean government lies with private houses—an image of high and low undistinguished.'
translations.idiomatic: Sima Biao read two heads as power trapped in private cliques, high and low blurred.

sentences.zh: 」京房《易傳》曰：「足多者，所任邪也；

translations.literal: ' Jing Fang’s Treatise on the Changes says: 'Many feet mean those employed are wicked;
translations.idiomatic: Jing Fang adds that too many feet mean wicked ministers hold office;

sentences.zh: 足少者，不勝任也。

translations.literal: few feet mean they cannot bear the charge.'
translations.idiomatic: too few mean they cannot bear their tasks.'

sentences.zh: 」其後王敦等亂政，此其祥也。

translations.literal: ' Afterward Wang Dun and others threw government into chaos—this was its auspice.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun’s revolt followed as the omen predicted.

sentences.zh: 四年十二月，郊牛死。

translations.literal: Fourth year, twelfth month: the suburban ox died.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of the fourth year the suburban-sacrifice ox died.

sentences.zh: 案劉向說《春秋》效牛死曰：「宣公區霿昏亂，故天不饗其祀。

translations.literal: According to Liu Xiang’s gloss on the Spring and Autumn effect of an ox dying: 'Duke Xuan was fog-dark and confused; therefore Heaven did not feast on his sacrifice.'
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xiang cites Duke Xuan’s moral fog that cost him heaven’s acceptance at sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 」今元帝中興之業，實王導之謀也。

translations.literal: ' Now the enterprise of Yuan’s restoration was in truth Wang Dao’s plan.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Yuan’s restoration rested on Wang Dao’s counsel.

sentences.zh: 劉隗探會上意，以得親幸，導見疏外，此區霿不睿之禍。

translations.literal: Liu Wei probed the sovereign’s mood to win favor, while Dao was pushed aside—this was the disaster of fog-dark lack of wisdom.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Wei’s flattery and Wang Dao’s exile matched the unwise-ruler omen.

sentences.zh: 成帝五月，護軍牛生犢，兩頭六足。

translations.literal: Chengdi, fifth month: the protector army’s ox calved a calf with two heads and six feet.
translations.idiomatic: In Cheng’s fifth month a guard command cow bore a six-legged two-headed calf.

sentences.zh: 是冬，蘇峻作亂。

translations.literal: That winter Su Jun raised rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Su Jun rebelled that winter.

sentences.zh: 七年，九德人袁榮家牛產犢，兩頭八足，二尾共身。

translations.literal: Seventh year: the man Yuan Rong of Jiude had a household ox calve a calf with two heads, eight feet, and two tails on one body.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year Yuan Rong of Jiude saw a two-headed eight-legged calf born.

sentences.zh: 桓玄之國，在荊州詣刺史殷仲堪，行至鶴穴，逢一老公驅青牛，形色瑰異，桓玄即以所乘牛易取。

translations.literal: When Huan Xuan went to Jingzhou to visit Inspector Yin Zhongkan, traveling to Crane Grotto he met an old man driving a green ox of strange form; Huan Xuan immediately traded his own mount for it.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Xuan swapped mounts with a strange old man at Crane Grotto on his way to see Yin Zhongkan.

sentences.zh: 乘至零陵涇溪，駿駛非常，息駕飲牛，牛逕入江水不出。

translations.literal: Riding to Jingxi in Lingling, it galloped extraordinarily fast; when he halted to water the ox, it went straight into the river and did not come out.
translations.idiomatic: At Lingling’s Jingxi the beast bolted into the river and vanished.

sentences.zh: 玄遣人覘守，經日無所見。

translations.literal: Xuan sent men to watch; after a full day nothing was seen.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Xuan’s watchers found nothing after a day.

sentences.zh: 于後玄敗被誅。

translations.literal: Later Xuan was defeated and executed.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Xuan later died under the blade.

translations.literal: Equals sign layout marker.
translations.idiomatic: Column divider.

sentences.zh: 黃眚黃祥

translations.literal: Yellow ill-omens and yellow portents.
translations.idiomatic: Section heading: yellow bale and yellow auspice.

sentences.zh: =蜀劉備，東伐。

translations.literal: Shu: Liu Bei campaigned eastward.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei of Shu marched east.

sentences.zh: 二月，自秭歸進屯夷道。

translations.literal: Second month: from Zigui he advanced and encamped at Yidao.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month he moved from Zigui to Yidao.

sentences.zh: 六月，秭歸有黃氣見，長十餘里，廣數十丈。

translations.literal: Sixth month: at Zigui yellow qi appeared, more than ten li long and tens of zhang wide.
translations.idiomatic: In June a yellow band of mist stretched ten-odd li along the sky at Zigui.

sentences.zh: 後逾旬，備為陸議所破，近黃祥也。

translations.literal: After more than a ten-day period Bei was defeated by Lu Yi—near a yellow portent.
translations.idiomatic: Within ten days Liu Bei lost to Lu Xun—a yellow omen fulfilled.

sentences.zh: 魏齊王正始中，中山王周南為襄邑長。

translations.literal: Wei Prince of Qi, Zhengshi era: Zhou Nan of Zhongshan was magistrate of Xiangyi.
translations.idiomatic: Under Wei’s Qi prince, Zhou Nan of Zhongshan served as Xiangyi magistrate.

sentences.zh: 有鼠從穴出，語曰：「王周南，爾以某日死。

translations.literal: A rat came from a hole and said: 'Wang Zhou Nan, you will die on such-and-such a day.'
translations.idiomatic: A rat emerged and prophesied Zhou Nan’s death date.

sentences.zh: 」周南不應，鼠還穴。

translations.literal: ' Zhou Nan did not answer; the rat returned to its hole.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Nan ignored the rat, which slipped back into its burrow.

sentences.zh: 後至期，更冠幘皁衣出，語曰：「周南，汝日中當死。

translations.literal: When the time came, it came out again wearing cap and black robes and said: 'Zhou Nan, you will die at noon.'
translations.idiomatic: On the appointed day the rat reappeared in black cap and robe to renew the noon death threat.

sentences.zh: 」又不應，鼠復入穴。

translations.literal: ' Again he did not answer; the rat again entered the hole.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Nan stayed silent and the rat withdrew again.

sentences.zh: 斯須更出，語如向。

translations.literal: In a moment it came out again, speaking as before.
translations.idiomatic: Moments later it repeated the same words.

sentences.zh: 日適欲中，鼠入須臾復出，出復入，轉更數，語如前。

translations.literal: As noon neared, the rat entered; after a moment it came out again, went in again, repeating several times, speaking as before.
translations.idiomatic: The rat darted in and out as noon approached, repeating its warning.

sentences.zh: 日適中，鼠曰：「周南，汝不應，我復何道！

translations.literal: When noon arrived, the rat said: 'Zhou Nan, you do not answer—what more can I say!'
translations.idiomatic: At noon it cried that Zhou Nan’s silence left nothing more to say.

sentences.zh: 」言絕，顛蹶而死，即失衣冠。

translations.literal: ' When the words ended, it fell over dead and at once lost its cap and clothes.
translations.idiomatic: It fell dead and shed its human-like garb.

sentences.zh: 取視，俱如常鼠。

translations.literal: When they took and looked, both were like ordinary rats.
translations.idiomatic: The corpse was an ordinary rat.

sentences.zh: 案班固說，此黃祥也。

translations.literal: According to Ban Gu’s gloss, this was a yellow portent.
translations.idiomatic: Ban Gu classed it as a yellow omen.

sentences.zh: 是時，曹爽專政，競為比周，故鼠作變也。

translations.literal: At this time Cao Shuang monopolized power; they vied in forming cliques; therefore the rat made this transformation.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Shuang’s clique-ridden rule drew the talking rat.

sentences.zh: 惠帝十二月，大霧。

translations.literal: Huidi, twelfth month: great fog.
translations.idiomatic: In Emperor Hui’s twelfth month heavy fog blanketed the land.

sentences.zh: 帝時昏眊，政非已出，故有區霿之妖。

translations.literal: The emperor was then dim-sighted; government did not issue from himself; therefore there was the prodigy of fog-darkness.
translations.idiomatic: The helpless emperor’s fog matched a court he could not see.

sentences.zh: 元帝八月，黃霧四寒，埃氛蔽天。

translations.literal: Yuandi, eighth month: yellow fog blocked the four quarters; dust haze veiled heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Yellow mist choked the horizon in Yuan’s eighth month.

sentences.zh: 十月，京師大霧，黑氣貫天，日無光。

translations.literal: Tenth month: in the capital great fog; black qi pierced heaven; the sun had no light.
translations.idiomatic: In October black vapor swallowed the capital sun.

sentences.zh: 明帝正月癸巳，黃霧四塞。

translations.literal: Mingdi, first month, day guisi: yellow fog blocked the four quarters.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi in Ming’s first month yellow fog returned.

sentences.zh: 二月，又黃霧四塞。

translations.literal: Second month: again yellow fog blocked the four quarters.
translations.idiomatic: February brought another yellow smother.

sentences.zh: 是時王敦擅權，謀逆愈甚。

translations.literal: At this time Wang Dun monopolized power; his plot of rebellion grew worse.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun’s treason thickened with the mist.

sentences.zh: 穆帝三月，涼州大風拔木，黃霧下塵。

translations.literal: Mudi, third month: in Liangzhou great wind uprooted trees; yellow fog lowered dust.
translations.idiomatic: In Mu’s third month Liangzhou saw gales and yellow dust fall from the sky.

sentences.zh: 是時，張重華納譖，出謝艾為酒泉太守，而所任非其人，至九年死，嗣子見殺，是其應也。

translations.literal: At this time Zhang Chonghua believed slander and sent Xie Ai out to be governor of Jiuquan, while those employed were not the right men; by the ninth year he died and the heir son was killed—this was its response.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chonghua’s purge of Xie Ai and bad appointments led to his death and his heir’s murder within nine years.

sentences.zh: 京房《易傳》曰：「聞善不予茲謂不知，厥異黃，厥咎聾，厥災不嗣。

translations.literal: Jing Fang’s Treatise on the Changes says: 'Hearing of good yet not awarding it is called lack of knowledge; its anomaly is yellow; its reproof is deafness; its disaster is no heirs.
translations.idiomatic: Jing Fang links yellow haze to refusing to reward merit.

sentences.zh: 黃者，有黃濁氣四塞天下。

translations.literal: Yellow means there is turbid yellow qi blocking the four quarters of the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Yellow means murky vapor filling the world.

sentences.zh: 蔽賢絕道，災至絕世也。」

translations.literal: Blocking worthies and cutting off the Way brings disaster to the point of cutting off generations.'
translations.idiomatic: Blocking worthies ends the dynasty’s line.'

sentences.zh: 孝武二月癸未，黃霧四塞。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu, second month, day guiwei: yellow fog blocked the four quarters.
translations.idiomatic: On guiwei in Emperor Wu’s second month yellow fog returned.

sentences.zh: 是時，道子專政，親近佞人，朝綱方替。

translations.literal: At this time Prince of Kuaiji Daozi held power, drew near sycophants, and court norms were collapsing.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Daozi’s faction and flatterers were rotting the court.

sentences.zh: 安帝十月丙申朔，黃霧昏濁不雨。

translations.literal: Andi, tenth month, new moon bingshen: yellow fog, murky and dark, without rain.
translations.idiomatic: On the bingshen new moon of Emperor An’s tenth month yellow murk hung without rain.

sentences.zh: 是時桓玄謀逆之應。

translations.literal: This was the response to Huan Xuan’s plot of usurpation.
translations.idiomatic: It answered Huan Xuan’s rising treason.

sentences.zh: 十一月，大霧。

translations.literal: Eleventh month: great fog.
translations.idiomatic: November brought dense fog.

sentences.zh: 十年十一月，又大霧。

translations.literal: Tenth year, eleventh month: again great fog.
translations.idiomatic: The eleventh month of the tenth year saw fog again.

sentences.zh: 是時，帝室衰微，臣下權盛，兵及土地，略非君有，此其應也。

translations.literal: At this time the imperial house was feeble; ministers’ power was strong; arms reached to the soil—territory was scarcely the lord’s; this was its response.
translations.idiomatic: The feeble throne and grasping ministers matched the omen.

translations.literal: Equals sign layout marker.
translations.idiomatic: Column divider.

sentences.zh: 地震

translations.literal: Earthquake.
translations.idiomatic: Section heading: seismic portents.

sentences.zh: =劉向曰：「地震，金木水火沴土者也。

translations.literal: Liu Xiang said: 'Earthquake is metal, wood, fire, and water encroaching on earth.'
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xiang read quakes as the four phases striking earth.

sentences.zh: 伯陽甫曰：「天地之氣，不過其序；

translations.literal: Boyang Fu said: 'The qi of heaven and earth does not overstep its sequence;
translations.idiomatic: Boyang Fu said heaven and earth keep an order;

sentences.zh: 若過其序，人之亂也。

translations.literal: if it oversteps the sequence, it is the disorder of men.'
translations.idiomatic: when that order breaks, human affairs are in chaos.'

sentences.zh: 陽伏而不能出，陰迫而不能升，於是有地震。」

translations.literal: Yang lies hidden and cannot emerge; yin presses and cannot rise—then there are earthquakes.'
translations.idiomatic: Trapped yang and pressing yin produce earthquakes.'

sentences.zh: 吳孫權，江東地連震。

translations.literal: Wu Sun Quan: the land east of the River shook in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Wu’s lands quaked repeatedly under Sun Quan.

sentences.zh: 是時，權受魏爵命為大將軍、吳王，改元專制，不修臣跡。

translations.literal: At this time Quan had received Wei’s patent as grand general and King of Wu, changed era names and acted on his own, and did not cultivate a minister’s demeanor.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan took Wei’s patent yet ruled like an independent king.

sentences.zh: 京房《易傳》曰：「臣事雖正，專必震。

translations.literal: Jing Fang’s Treatise on the Changes says: 'Though a minister’s service is correct, if he monopolizes power there must be shaking.'
translations.idiomatic: Jing Fang warns that ministerial monopoly brings tremors.

sentences.zh: 其震，于水則波，於木則搖，於屋則瓦落。

translations.literal: Its shaking: in water it makes waves; in wood it makes swaying; in houses it makes tiles fall.
translations.idiomatic: Such shaking stirs water, bends trees, and drops roof tiles.

sentences.zh: 大經在辟而易臣茲謂陰動，厥震搖政宮。

translations.literal: When the great norm rests with the ruler yet ministers are easily changed, this is called yin stirring; its shaking sways the halls of government.
translations.idiomatic: When law sits with the throne but ministers are swapped lightly, palace halls shake.

sentences.zh: 大經搖政茲謂不陰，厥震搖山，出湧水。

translations.literal: When the great norm shakes government, this is called not yin; its shaking sways mountains and sends gushing water.
translations.idiomatic: When the norm itself totters, mountains slide and springs burst forth.

sentences.zh: 嗣子無德專祿茲謂不順，厥震動丘陵，湧水出。

translations.literal: When the heir son lacks virtue yet monopolizes emolument, this is called non-compliance; its shaking moves hillocks and gushing water comes out.
translations.idiomatic: Heirs without virtue yet clinging to salary shake hills and loose floods.

sentences.zh: 」劉向並云：「臣下強盛，將動而為害之應也。」

translations.literal: ' Liu Xiang together said: 'When ministers below are strong, it is the response that they will move and do harm.'
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xiang concludes that ministerial strength foretells destructive upheaval.'

sentences.zh: 魏明帝十一月，京都地震，從東來，隱隱有聲，搖屋瓦。

translations.literal: Wei Mingdi, eleventh month: the capital earthquake came from the east, dimly rumbling, shaking roof tiles.
translations.idiomatic: In Ming’s eleventh month Luoyang felt an eastern tremor that rattled tiles.

sentences.zh: 六月戊申，京都地震。

translations.literal: Sixth month, day wushen: capital earthquake.
translations.idiomatic: On wushen in the sixth month the capital shook again.

sentences.zh: 是秋，吳將朱然圍江夏，荊州刺史胡質擊退之。

translations.literal: That autumn Wu general Zhu Ran besieged Jiangxia; Jingzhou Inspector Hu Zhi repelled him.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn Zhu Ran besieged Jiangxia until Hu Zhi drove him off.

sentences.zh: 又，公孫文懿叛，自立為燕王，改年，置百官。

translations.literal: Also, Gongsun Yuan (posthumously Wenyi) rebelled, set himself up as King of Yan, changed the era, and installed officials.
translations.idiomatic: Gongsun Yuan rose as king of Yan, adopted a new reign title, and filled out a court.

sentences.zh: 明年，討平之。

translations.literal: The next year he was campaigned against and pacified.
translations.idiomatic: He was crushed the next year.

sentences.zh: 吳孫權五月，江東地震。

translations.literal: Wu Sun Quan, fifth month: the land east of the River earthquake.
translations.idiomatic: In Sun Quan’s fifth month eastern Wu quaked.

sentences.zh: 正月，地再震。

translations.literal: First month: the earth shook again.
translations.idiomatic: The first month brought another tremor.

sentences.zh: 是時，呂壹專事，步騭上疏曰：「伏聞校事吹毛求瑕，趣欲陷人，成其威福，無罪無辜，橫受重刑，雖有大臣，不見信任，如此，天地焉得無變！

translations.literal: At this time Lü Yi monopolized affairs; Bu Zhi submitted a memorial saying: 'I have heard that the investigator-officials blow on hairs seeking flaws, eager to trap men and complete their power and blessing; guiltless innocents suffer extreme punishments; though there are great ministers, they are not trusted—in such a case how can heaven and earth be without change!'
translations.idiomatic: Lü Yi’s investigators, says Bu Zhi’s memorial, hunted petty faults, framed the innocent, and left great ministers untrusted—small wonder heaven and earth shuddered.

sentences.zh: 故地連震動，臣下專政之應也。
冀所以警悟人主，可不深思其意哉！
」壹後卒敗。
魏齊王十一月，南安郡地震。
三年七月甲申，南安郡地震。
十二月，魏郡地震。
六年二月丁卯，南安郡地震。
是時，曹爽專政，遷太后于永甯宮，太后與帝相泣而別。
連年地震，是其應也。
吳孫權二月，江東地仍震。
是時，權聽讒，尋黜硃據，廢太子。
蜀劉禪，蜀地震。
是時宦人黃皓專權。
案司馬彪說，「閹官無陽施，猶婦人也」。
皓見任之應，與漢和帝時同事也。
是冬，蜀亡。
武帝四月辛酉，地震。
是年冬，新平氐羌叛。
明年，孫皓遣大眾入渦口。
七年六月丙申，地震。
八月庚辰，河南、河東、平陽地震。
四年六月丁未，陰平廣武地震，甲子又震。
二月庚申，淮南、丹陽地震。
五年正月朔壬辰，京師地震。
六年七月己丑，地震。
七年七月，南安、犍為地震。
八月，京兆地震。
八年五月壬子，建安地震。
七月，陰平地震。
八月，丹陽地震。
九年正月，會稽、丹陽、吳興地震。
四月辛酉，長沙、南海等郡國八地震。
七月至於八月，地又四震，其三有聲如雷。
九月，臨賀地震，十二月又震。
十年十二月己亥，丹楊地震。
正月，地又震，武帝世，始于賈充，終於楊駿，阿黨昧利，苟竊朝權。
至於末年，所任轉弊，故頻年地震，過其序也，終喪天下。
惠帝十二月辛酉，京都地震。
此夏，賈后使楚王瑋殺汝南王亮及太保衛瓘，此陰道盛、陽道微故也。
四年二月，上穀、上庸、遼東地震。
五月，蜀郡山移；
淮南壽春洪水出，山崩地陷，壞城府。
八月，上谷地震，水出，殺百餘人。
十月，京都地震。
十一月，滎陽、襄城、汝陰、梁國、南陽地皆震。
十二月，京都又震。
是時，賈后亂朝，終至禍敗之應也。
漢鄧太后攝政時，郡國地震。
李固以為：「地，陰也，法當安靜。
今乃越陰之職，專陽之政，故應以震。
」此同事也。
京房《易傳》曰：「小人剝廬，厥妖山崩，茲謂陰乘陽，弱勝強。
」又曰：「陰背陽則地裂，父子分離，夷羌叛去。」
五年五月丁丑，地震。
六月，金城地震。
六年正月丁丑，地震。
八年正月丙辰，地震。
十月，地震。
時齊王冏專政之應。
二年十二月丙辰，地震。
是時，長沙王乂專政之應也。
孝杯帝十月，荊、湘二州地震。
時司馬越專政。
四年四月，兗州地震。
五月，石勒寇汲郡，執太守胡寵，遂南濟河，是其應也。
湣帝四月甲辰，地震。
三年六月丁卯，長安又地震。
是時主幼，權傾于下，四方雲擾，兵亂不息之應也。
元帝四月，西平地震，湧水出。
十二月，廬陵、豫章、武昌、西陵地震，湧水出，山崩。
干寶以為王敦陵上之應也。
二年五月己丑，祁山地震，山崩，殺人。
是時，相國南陽王保在祁山，稱晉王不終之象也。
三年五月庚寅，丹陽、吳郡、晉陵又地震。
成帝二月，江陵地震。
三月，益州地震。
四月己未，豫章地震。
是年，蘇峻作亂。
九年三月丁酉，會稽地震。
穆帝六月癸亥，地震。
是時，嗣主幼沖，母后稱制，政在臣下，所以連年地震。
二年十月，地震。
三年正月丙辰，地震。
九月，地又震。
四年十月己未，地震。
五年正月庚寅，地震。
是時，石季龍僭即皇帝位，亦過其序也。
九年八月丁酉，京都地震，有聲如雷。
十年正月丁卯，地震，聲如雷，雞雉皆鳴呴。
十一年四月乙酉，地震。
五月丁未，地震。
升平二年十一月辛酉，地震。
五年八月，涼州地震。
哀帝四月甲戌，地震。
是時，政在將相，人主南面而已。
興甯元年四月甲戌，揚州地震，湖瀆溢。
二年二月庚寅，江陵地震。
是時，桓溫專政。
海西公二月，涼州地震，水湧。
是海西將廢之應也。
簡文帝十月辛未，安成地震。
是年帝崩。
孝武帝甯康元年十月辛未，地震。
二年二月丁巳，地震。
七月甲午，涼州地又震，山崩。
是時，嗣主幼沖，權在將相，陰盛之應也。
閏三月壬午，地震。
五月丁丑，地震。
十一年六月己卯，地震。
是後緣河諸將連歲兵役，人勞之應也。
十五年二月己酉朔夜，地震。
八月，京都地震。
十二月己未，地震。
十七年六月癸卯，地震。
十二月己未，地又震。
是時，群小弄權，天下側目。
十八年正月癸亥朔，地震。
二月乙未夜，地震。
安帝四月乙未，地震。
九月癸丑，地震。
是時，幼主沖昧，政在臣下。
正月壬子夜，地震有聲。
十月癸亥，地震。
五年正月戊戌夜，尋陽地震，有聲如雷。
明年，盧循下。
八年，自正月至四月，南康、廬陵地四震。
明年，王旅西討荊益。
十年三月戊寅，地震。
山崩地陷裂
=吳孫權八月，丹陽、句容及故鄣、甯國諸山崩，鴻水溢。
案劉向說，「山，陽，君也。
水，陰，百姓也。
天戒若曰，君道崩壞，百姓將失其所與」！
春秋梁山崩，漢齊、楚眾山發水，同事也。
夫三代命祀，祭不越望，吉凶禍福，不是過也。
吳雖稱帝，其實列國，災發丹陽，其天意矣。
劉歆以為：「國主山川，山崩川竭，亡之徵也。
」後二年而權薨，又二十六年而吳亡。
魏元帝二月，太行山崩，此魏亡之徵也。
其冬，晉有天下。
武帝三月戊午，大石山崩。
四年七月，泰山崩墜三里。
京房《易傳》曰：「自上下者為崩，厥應泰山之石顛而下，聖王受命人君虜。
」及帝晏駕，而祿去王室，惠皇懦弱，懷湣二帝俱辱虜庭，淪胥於北，元帝中興于南，此其應也。
五月丙午，宣帝廟地陷。
六年十月，南安新興山崩，湧水出。
七年二月，硃提之大瀘山崩，震壞郡舍，陰平之仇池崖隕。
八年七月，大雨，殿前地陷，方五尺，深數丈，中有破船。
惠帝，蜀郡山崩，殺人。
五月壬子，壽春山崩，洪水出，城壞，地陷方三十丈，殺人。
六月，壽春大雷，山崩地坼，人家陷死，上庸亦如之。
八月，居庸地裂，廣三十六丈，長八十四丈，水出，大饑。
上庸四處山崩，地墜廣三十丈，長百三十丈，水出殺人。
皆賈后亂朝之應也。
四月，西墉崩。
懷帝三月，洛陽東北步廣裏地陷。
二年八月乙亥，鄄城城無故自壞七十餘丈，司馬越惡之，遷于濮陽，此見沴之異也。
越卒以陵上受禍。
三年七月戊辰，當陽地裂三所，廣三丈，長三百餘步。
京房《易傳》曰：「地坼裂者，臣下分離，不肯相從也。
」其後司馬越苟晞交惡，四方牧伯莫不離散，王室遂亡。
三年十月，宜都夷道山崩。
四年四月，湘東[需阝]黑石山崩。
元帝二月，廬陵、豫章、武昌，西陽地震山崩。
二年五月，祁山地震，山崩，殺人。
三年，南平郡山崩，出雄黃數千斤。
時王敦陵傲，帝優容之，示含養禍萌也。
四年八月，常山崩，水出，滹沲盈溢，大木傾拔。
成帝十月，柴桑廬山西北崖崩。
十二月，劉胤為郭默所殺。
穆帝九月，峻平、崇陽二陵崩。
十二年十一月，遣散騎常侍車灌修峻平陵，開埏道，崩壓，殺數十人。
升平五年二月，南掖門馬足陷地，得鐘一，有文四字。
哀帝四月丁丑，浩亹山崩，張天錫亡徵也。
安帝三月壬寅，山陰地陷，方四丈，有聲如雷。
十年五月戊寅，西明門地穿，湧水出，毀門扇及限，此水沴土也。
十一年五月，霍山崩，出銅鐘六枚。
十三年七月，漢中成固縣水涯有聲若雷，既而岸崩，出銅鐘十有二枚。
惠帝六月夜，暴雷雨，賈謐齋屋柱陷入地，壓謐床帳，此木沴土，土失其性，不能載也。
明年，謐誅焉。
五月，范陽國地燃，可以爨，此火沴土也。
是時，禮樂征伐自諸候出。
皇之不極，是謂不建
《傳》曰：「皇之不極，是謂不建，厥咎眊，厥罰恆陰，厥極弱。
時則有射妖，時則有龍蛇之孽，時則有馬禍，時則有下人伐上之痾，時則有日月亂行，星辰逆行。
」皇之不極，是謂不建。
皇，君；
極，中；
建，立也。
人君貌言視聽思心五事皆失，不得其中，不能立萬事，失在眊悖，故其咎眊也。
王者自下承天理物。
雲起於山，而彌於天；
天氣亂，故其罰恆陰，一曰：「上失中，則下強盛而蔽君明也。
」《易》曰：「亢龍有悔，貴而亡位，高而亡民，賢人在下位而亡輔。
」如此，則君有南面之尊，而亡一人之助，故其極弱也。
盛陽動進輕疾。
禮，春而大射，以順陽氣。
上微弱則下奮驚動，故有射妖。
《易》曰：「雲從龍。
」又曰：「龍蛇之蟄，以存身也。
」陰氣動，故有龍蛇之孽。
于《易》，乾為君，為馬。
任用而強力，君氣毀，故有馬禍。
一曰，馬多死及為怪，亦是也。
君亂且弱，人之所叛，天之所去，不有明王之誅，則有篡殺之禍，故有下人伐上之痾。
凡君道傷者，病天氣。
不言五行沴天，而曰「日月亂行，星辰逆行」者，為若下不敢沴天，猶《春秋》曰「王師敗績於貿戎」，不言敗之者，以自敗為文，尊尊之意也。
劉歆《皇極傳》曰有下體生於上之痾。
說以為下人伐上，天誅已成，不得復為痾云。
恆陰
=吳孫亮，自八月沈陰不雨，四十餘日。
是時，將誅孫綝，謀泄。
九月戊午，綝以兵圍宮，廢亮為會稽王，此恆陰之罰也。
吳孫皓十二月，太史奏久陰不雨，將有陰謀。
孫皓驚懼。
時陸凱等謀因其謁廟廢之。
及出，留平領兵前驅，凱先語平，平不許，是以不果。
皓既肆虐，群下多懷異圖，終至降亡
射妖
=蜀車騎將軍鄧芝征涪陵，見玄猨緣山，手射中之。
猨拔其箭，卷木葉塞其創。
芝曰：「嘻！
吾違物之性，其將死矣！
」俄而卒，此射妖也。
一曰，猨母抱子，芝射中之，子為拔箭，取木葉塞創。
芝歎息，投弩水中，自知當死。
恭帝為琅邪王，好奇戲，嘗閑一馬於門內，令人射之，欲觀幾箭死，左右有諫者曰：「馬，國姓也。
今射之，不祥。
」於是乃止，而馬已被十許箭矣。
此蓋射妖也。
俄而禪位於宋焉。
龍蛇之孽
=魏明帝正月甲申，青龍見郟之摩陂井中。
凡瑞興非時，則為妖孽，況困于井，非嘉祥矣。
魏以改年，非也。
干寶曰：「自明帝，終魏世，青龍、黃龍見者，皆其主興廢之應也。
魏土運，青木色，而不勝於金。
黃得位，青失位之象也。
青能多見者，君德國運內相克伐也。
故高貴鄉公卒敗於兵。
」案劉向說，龍貴象而困井中，諸侯將有幽執之禍也。
魏世，龍莫不在井，此居上者逼制之應。
高貴鄉公著《潛龍詩》，即此旨也。
高貴鄉公十月戊戌，黃龍見於鄴井中。
正月辛丑，青龍見軹縣井中。
六月乙丑，青龍見元城縣界井中。
二年二月，青龍見溫縣井中。
三年，黃龍、青龍俱見頓丘、冠軍、陽夏縣界井中。
四年正月，黃龍二見寧陵縣界井中。
元帝十二月甲申，黃龍見華陰縣井中。
三年二月，龍見軹縣井中。
吳孫皓天冊中，龍乳于長沙人家，啖雞雛。
京房《易妖》曰：「龍乳人家，王者為庶人。
」其後皓降晉。
武帝六月丙午，白龍二見於九原井中。
正月癸卯，二龍見武庫井中。
帝觀之，有喜色。
百僚將賀，劉毅獨表曰：「昔龍漦夏庭，禍發周室。
龍見鄭門，子產不賀。
」帝答曰：「朕德政未修，未有以應受嘉祥。
」遂不賀也。
孫盛曰：「龍，水物也，何與於人！
子產言之當矣。
但非其所處，實為妖災。
夫龍以飛翔顯見為瑞，今則潛伏幽處，非休祥也。
」漢惠帝二年，兩龍見蘭陵井中，本志以為其後趙王幽死之象。
武庫者，帝王威禦之器所寶藏也，屋宇邃密，非龍所處。
是後七年，籓王相害，二十八年，果有二胡僭竊神器，二逆皆字曰龍，此之表異，為有證矣。
湣帝十一月，枹罕羌妓產一龍子，色似錦，文常就母乳，遙見神光，少得就視。
此亦皇之不建，於是帝竟淪沒。
呂纂末，龍出東廂井中，到其殿前蟠臥，比旦失之。
俄又有黑龍升其宮門。
纂咸以為美瑞。
或曰：「龍者陰類，出入有時，今而屢見，必有下人謀上之變。
」後纂果為呂超所殺。
武帝咸甯中，司徒府有二大蛇，長十許丈，居聽事平橑上而人不知，但數年怪府中數失小兒及豬犬之屬。
後有一蛇夜出，被刃傷不能去，乃覺之，發徒攻擊，移時乃死。
夫司徒，五教之府；
此皇極不建，故蛇孽見之。
漢靈帝時，蛇見御座，楊賜云為帝溺于色之應也。
魏代宮人猥多，晉又過之，燕遊是湎，此其孽也。
《詩》云「惟虺惟蛇，女子之祥」也。
惠帝三月癸巳，臨淄有大蛇，長十餘丈，負二小蛇入城北門，逕從市入漢城陽景王祠中，不見。
天戒若曰，昔漢景王有定傾之功，而不厲節忠慎，以至失職奪功之辱。
今齊王冏不寤，雖建興復之功，而驕陵取禍，此其徵也。
明帝太甯初，武昌有大蛇，常居故神祠空樹中，每出頭從人受食。
京房《易妖》曰：「蛇見於邑，不出三年有大兵，國有大憂。
」尋有王敦之逆。
馬禍
=武帝，遼東有馬生角，在兩耳下，長三寸。
案劉向說曰，「此兵象也」。
及帝晏駕之後，王室毒於兵禍，是其應也。
京房《易傳》曰：「臣易上，政不順，厥妖馬生角，茲謂賢士不足。
」又曰：「天子親伐，馬生角。
」《呂氏春秋》曰：「人君失道，馬有生角。
」及惠帝踐阼，昏愚失道，又親征伐成都，是其應也。
惠帝十二月，皇太子將釋奠，太傅趙王倫驂乘，至南城門，馬止，力士推之不能動。
倫入軺車，乃進。
此馬禍也。
天戒若曰，倫不知義方，終為亂逆，非傅導行禮之人也。
九年十一月戊寅，忽有牡騮馬驚奔至廷尉訊堂，悲鳴而死。
天戒若曰，湣懷冤死之象也。
見廷尉訊堂，其天意乎！
懷帝二月，神馬鳴南城門。
湣帝九月，蒲子縣馬生人。
京房《易傳》曰：「上亡天子，諸侯相伐，厥妖馬生人。
」是時，帝室衰微，不絕如線，胡狄交侵，兵戈日逼，尋而帝亦淪陷，故此妖見也。
元帝，丹陽郡吏濮陽演馬生駒，兩頭，自項前別，生而死。
司馬彪說曰：「此政在私門，二頭之象也。
」其後王敦陵上。
成帝五月甲戌，有馬色赤如血，自宣陽門直走入於殿前，盤旋走出，尋逐，莫知所在。
己卯，帝不豫。
六月，崩。
此馬禍，又赤祥也。
是年，張重華在涼州，將誅其西河相張祚，廄馬數十匹，同時悉無後尾也。
安帝十月，梁州有馬生角，刺史郭銓送示桓玄。
案劉向說曰，馬不當生角，猶玄不當舉兵向上也。
玄不寤，以至夷滅。
石季龍在鄴，有一馬尾有燒狀，入其中陽門，出顯陽門，東宮皆不得入，走向東北，俄爾不見。
術者佛圖澄歎曰：「災其及矣！
」逾年季龍死，其國遂滅。
人痾
=魏文帝黃初，清河宋士宗母化為鱉，入水。
明帝，曹休部曲丘奚農女死復生。
時又有開周世塚，得殉葬女子，數日而有氣，數月而不能言，郭太后愛養之。
又，太原人發塚破棺，棺中有一生婦人，問其本事，不知也，視其墓木，可三十歲。
案京房《易傳》曰：「至陰為陽，下人為上。
」宣帝起之象也。
漢平帝、獻帝並有此異，占以為王莽、曹操之徵。
孫休，安吳民陳焦死七日復生，穿塚出。
干寶曰：「此與漢宣帝同事，烏程侯皓承廢故之家，得位之祥也。」
孫皓，丹陽宣騫母年八十，因浴化為黿，兄弟閉戶衛之。
掘堂上作大坎，實水其中，黿入坎遊戲，一二日恆延頸外望。
伺戶小開，便輪轉自躍，入於遠潭，遂不復還。
與漢靈帝時黃氏母同事，吳亡之象也。
魏元帝八月，襄武縣言有大人見，長三丈餘，跡長三尺二寸，髮白，著黃巾黃單衣，柱杖呼王始語曰：「今當太平。
」晉尋代魏。
武帝，元城人年七十生角。
殆趙王倫篡亂之象也。
十二月，琅邪人顏畿病死，棺斂已久，家人咸夢畿謂己曰；
「我當復生，可急開棺。
」遂出之，漸能飲食屈伸視瞻，不能行語，二年復死。
京房《易傳》曰：「至陰為陽，下人為上，厥妖人死復生。
」其後劉元海、石勒僭逆，遂亡晉室，下為上之應也。
惠帝元康中，安豐有女子周世寧，年八歲，漸化為男，至十七八而氣性成。
京房《易傳》曰：「女子化為丈夫，茲謂陰昌，賤人為王。
」此亦劉元海、石勒蕩覆天下之妖也。
永甯初，齊王冏唱義兵，誅除亂逆，乘輿反正。
忽有婦人詣大司馬門求寄產，門者詰之，婦曰；
「我截臍便去耳。
」是時，齊王冏匡復王室，天下歸功，識者為其惡之，後果斬戮。
永甯元年十二月甲子，有白頭公入齊王冏大司馬府，大呼曰：「有大兵起，不出甲子旬。
」冏殺之。
明年十二月戊辰，冏敗，即甲子旬也。
四月癸酉，有人自雲龍門入殿前，北面再拜曰：「我當作中書監。
」即收斬之。
干寶以為「禁庭尊秘之處，今賤人徑入而門衛不覺者，宮室將虛而下人逾上之妖也」。
是後帝北遷鄴，又遷長安，宮闕遂空焉。
元康中，梁國女子許嫁，已受禮娉，尋而其夫戍長安，經年不歸，女家更以適人。
女不樂行，其父母逼強，不得已而去，尋得病亡。
後其夫還，問其女所在，其傢俱說之。
其夫逕至女墓，不勝哀情，便發塚開棺，女遂活，因與俱歸。
後婿聞知，詣官爭之，所在不能決。
秘書郎王導議曰：「此是非常事，不得以常理斷之，宜還前夫。
」朝廷從其議。
惠帝世，杜錫家葬而婢誤不得出，後十年開塚祔葬而婢尚生。
始如瞑，有頃漸覺，問之，自謂再宿耳。
初，婢之埋年十五六，及開塚更生，猶十五六也，嫁之有子。
，會稽謝真生子，頭大而有髮，兩蹠反向上，有男女兩體，生便作丈夫聲，經一日死。
此皇之不極，下人伐上之痾，於是諸王有僭亂之象也。
惠帝之世，京洛有人兼男女體，亦能兩用人道，而性尤淫，此亂氣所生。
自咸甯、太康之後，男寵大興，甚于女色，士大夫莫不尚之，天下相仿效，或至夫婦離絕，多生怨曠，故男女之氣亂而妖形作也。
懷帝，吳郡吳縣萬詳婢生子，鳥頭，兩足馬蹄，一手，無毛，尾黃色，大如枕。
此亦人妖，亂之象也。
五年五月，枹罕令嚴根妓產一龍，一女，一鵝。
京房《易傳》曰：「人生他物，非人所見者，皆為天下大兵。
」是時，帝承惠皇之後，四海沸騰，尋而陷於平陽，為逆胡所害，此其徵也。
湣帝，新蔡縣吏任僑妻產二女，腹與心相合，自胸以上、臍以下各分，此蓋天下未一之妖也。
時內史呂會上言：「案《瑞應圖》，異根同體謂之連理，異畝同穎謂之嘉禾。
草木之異猶以為瑞，今二人同心，《易》稱'二人同心，其利斷金'，蓋四海同心之瑞也。
」時皆哂之。
俄而四海分崩，帝亦淪沒。
元帝太興初，有女子其陰在腹，當臍下，自中國來至江東，其性淫而不產。
又有女子陰在首，渡在揚州，性亦淫。
京房《易妖》曰；
「人生子，陰在首，天下大亂；
在腹，天下有事；
在背，天下無後。
」于時王敦據上流，將欲為亂，是其徵。
三年十二月，尚書騶謝平妻生女，墮地濞濞有聲，須臾便死。
鼻目皆在頂上，面處如項，口有齒，都連為一，胸如鱉，手足爪如鳥爪，皆下勾。
此亦人生他物，非人所見者。
後二年，有石頭之敗。
明帝七月，丹陽江甯侯紀妻死，經三日復生。
成帝四月，下邳民王和僑居暨陽，息女可年二十，自云上天來還，得徵瑞印綬，當母天下。
晉陵太守以為妖，收付獄。
至十一月，有人持柘杖絳衣詣止車門，口列為聖人使求見天子。
門侯受辭，辭稱姓呂名賜，其言王和女可右足下有七星，星皆有毛，長七寸，天今命可為天下母。
奏聞，即伏誅，並下晉陵誅可。
康帝十月，衛將軍營督過望所領兵陳瀆女台有文在其足，曰「天下之母」，灸之愈明。
京都喧嘩，有司收系以聞。
俄自建康縣獄亡去。
明年，帝崩，獻後臨朝，此其祥也。
孝武帝甯康初，南郡州陵女唐氏漸化為丈夫。
安帝，無錫人趙未年八歲，一旦暴長八尺，髭須蔚然，三日而死。
義熙中，東陽人莫氏生女不養，埋之數日，於土中啼，取養遂活。
義熙末，吳豫章人有二陽道，重累生。
恭帝，建安人陽道無頭，正平，本下作女人形體。
